claims.text: The two-step thermal-mechanical treatment will induce a fine bimodal microstructure containing nanoscale coherent precipitates in a refined grain matrix.
This induced microstructure will synergistically improve strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance relative to the conventional as-cast state.
As-cast, homogenized CoCrFeMnNi has a single-phase, relatively coarse-grained structure lacking significant nanoscale precipitates.
Annealing CoCrFeMnNi at 650–750 °C for a controlled duration will nucleate nanoscale coherent precipitates.
Rapid quenching after annealing will freeze the precipitate-containing microstructure.
Light cold rolling after quenching will further refine the grain size while retaining the precipitate distribution.
Optimizing annealing temperature and duration will avoid precipitate coarsening.
The treatment should apply to CoCrFeMnNi-family and related high-entropy alloys having accessible precipitation kinetics in the 650–750 °C range.
The effect may fail when the alloy has insufficient thermodynamic driving force for precipitate formation.
Excessive annealing can cause precipitate coarsening and eliminate the beneficial effects.
Nanoscale precipitates hinder dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
The refined grain structure provides grain-boundary strengthening while maintaining or improving ductility.
Coherent precipitates provide effective load transfer that increases Young’s modulus.
The precipitate distribution arrests crack propagation and improves fracture resistance through crack-tip shielding and load transfer.
The treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The treatment will increase Young’s modulus by approximately 10–20% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The treatment will increase strain-to-failure by roughly 15% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The treatment will increase fracture toughness as measured by critical stress intensity factor.
The improvements occur only within a narrow annealing temperature-and-time window and are lost upon precipitate coarsening or dissolution.

contradictions.description: The initial and baseline material is described as homogenized, but the baseline is also described as having no post-casting thermal treatment; homogenization is itself a post-casting thermal treatment.
